newsitem.title: USA: Dominican president seeks to sell stakes in firms.
newsitem.headline: Dominican president seeks to sell stakes in firms.

text.p: Dominican Republic President Leonel Fernandez called for the sale of half-stakes in a wide range of state-owned enterprises, including the electric company.

The president, who was elected in June, said he had found little opposition in the Dominican Congress to the proposed sale of 50 percent of state firms to private interests that could make management more efficient.
"There is a recognition that you cannot go on with the status quo," Fernandez told reportors on his first visit to New York as president.
Fernandez described his government as following Bolivia's model of selling state firms. "I feel optimistic about this," Fernandez said about the legislative approval.
Fernandez said that, should the capitalization plan fail to win congressional approval, his administration would advocate privatization.

The public sector reforms would amount to $310 million in government holdings by the end of 1996, including the Dominican electricity corp, the Dominican Corp of State enterprises (CORDE) and seven sugar mills, a government release said.
The president said he expected completion of the electric company sale within five or six months.
"Much (of the government's budget deficit) has to do with the transfers of funds to state firms," Fernandez said.
